message.content: The new test file reveals the expected behavior: with empty columns, output is just the header line — rows contribute nothing. Let me fix my implementation and my own test.
message.reasoning_content:
The test test_export_extra.py asserts that with empty columns and one row, output is "
" — just the header (empty line), no row line. So when columns is empty, only the header is written and rows contribute nothing (an empty record would be an empty line, but expected output is just one "
").

Interesting — that's a design decision: with zero columns, each row produces... nothing? The expected output "
" means header only, rows skipped (or produce zero-length lines). My implementation wrote "

" (header + one empty record). Fix: when columns is empty, skip writing rows entirely (or equivalently, don't write the trailing empty record). Actually RFC 4180 would write an empty line per row, but the test says just "
".

Also my own test test_empty_columns expected "

" — I should update my test to match. Since my test file is optional and mine, I can edit it.

Fix export_csv: if not columns: return just the header line (or in general, only write rows if columns non-empty? No — better: if columns is empty, rows produce no output lines). Hmm, but what about empty rows AND empty columns → output "" or "
"? With header written, "
" would be output. The test only covers one row. Safest: header always written; each row writes a record only if columns non-empty. Actually with zero columns a record is an empty line — the test expects no line per row. So skip rows when columns is empty.
